title: Giants' Cam Skattebo putting his backflip on the back burner after seeing Aidan Hutchinson celebration injury
text:
The New York Giants running back said he's 'not doing that' anymore but left the door open for the playoffs

Aidan Hutchinson’s SELFISHNESS Just Cost The Lions A Super Bowl | The Craig Carton Show

On today’s Craig Carton show, Craig Carton reacts to the devastating news that Detroit Lions star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson is out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after suffering a torn ACL in his right knee

Cam Skattebo's signature touchdown celebration is officially on the shelf.

The New York Giants running back, who is much better known for his backflips after scoring than just about anything else he does on the football field, has apparently decided that celly can be catastrophic.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

So Skattebo doesn't see himself repeating the move any longer after watching Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson blow out his right knee during a sack celebration of Drake Maye last Sunday in Germany.

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo does a flip to celebrate after scoring a touchdown during the first half of an NFL game against the Washington Commanders in East Rutherford, N.J., Thursday, Nov. 12, 2026. (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

LIONS' STAR HURT CELEBRATING SACK OF PATRIOTS’ DRAKE MAYE AS BOTH INJURED ON POSSIBLY SEASON-ALTERING PLAY

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told a couple of reporters on Wednesday, according to the New York Post. "I'm saying, yeah [no more]. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.'

"That ain't going to happen to me."

This retirement of the backflip comes with caveats:

If he simply forgets and instincts take over, it might happen. And big moments like a Super Bowl win or something otherwise notable might bring back the flip.

"If we go to the playoffs or something," Skattebo said.

Aidan Hutchinson of the Detroit Lions goes down with an injury while celebrating a sack during an NFL game against the New England Patriots at Allianz Arena in Munich, Germany, on Nov. 15, 2026. (Getty Images)

Skattebo, it should be noted, is in only his second season with the Giants and has struggled with his share of injuries.

GIANTS' CAM SKATTEBO VOWS TO MAINTAIN VIOLENT PLAYING STYLE AFTER GRUESOME ANKLE INJURY

During Week 8 of the 2025 season against the Philadelphia Eagles, Skattebo suffered a gruesome right ankle injury. The trauma resulted in a dislocated ankle, a fractured fibula, and a ruptured deltoid ligament.

In October, Skattebo suffered a Grade 1 hamstring strain and missed one game as a result.

CAM SKATTEBO HORRIFIES GIANTS FANS BY ATTEMPTING A BACKFLIP DESPITE COMING OFF A LEG INJURY

New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo (44) leaves the field after an injury during the first half of an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday, Oct. 26, 2025, in Philadelphia. (AP Photo/Matt Rourke)

Despite the injuries, Skattebo previously defended continuing his backflips.

Following a viral incident where he botched a backflip on a bouncy WWE/Fanatics Fest floor — raising concerns because it came on the heels of last year's major injury — Skattebo brushed off suggestions he stop.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

He noted that he had been doing backflips since he was four years old and stated, "I will not hurt myself before the season."

In the 24-21 loss to the Washington Commanders on Nov. 12, Skattebo scored two touchdowns and after one of those he was actually joined by other teammates doing backflips.

It's unclear if group flipping is also going away.

Armando Salguero is OutKick's Senior NFL Writer.
